Will there be a bike? Progress report, model part¶

Team 3, MIE1517. For every Toronto Bike Share station we forecast the probability that at least one classic bike, and at least one e-bike, will be docked there h = 2–15 minutes from now.

Summary. [D1] Our best model so far is the MLP 2×256, dropout 0.3 network. On the validation days, on the station-times our table keeps (some count of classic bikes, e-bikes or free docks is 2 or less), it beats an honest 'what you see now' forecast (calibrated persistence) by a Brier skill score of 0.154 for classic bikes and 0.117 for e-bikes. Most of that is knowing the station and the hour: a look-up table that adds them (no learning) gets 0.115 / 0.085, and the network beats that table by 0.044 / 0.035. [D2] On the test days the skill against calibrated persistence is 0.125 / 0.092. For this model the test days were read once, for the chosen model only; the same days were scored once before (Nov 12) for our earlier count models, and nothing in this search was chosen on them. [D3] What is left: retrain on a larger dataset (data v2) whose test week nobody has read, longer history for the sequence models, and a rider-level evaluation; plan and dates in Section 8.

All prose below is a draft: blue text marked [Dn] is draft text, red text marked [Cn] is a claim still to be checked. Every number is printed from a table written by a script of the project.

Key findings¶

What we predict and how we score it

  1. [K1] We predict P(at least one bike at t + h) for each bike type: the question a rider has.
  2. [K2] The score is the skill against a reference forecast, skill = 1 − Brier_model / Brier_ref, with calibrated persistence (an honest 'what you see now' probability) as the reference: 0 = no better than the reference, 1 = perfect.

What the model learns, and where it helps (validation days)

  1. [K3] Knowing the station matters most: the chosen model, which knows it, reaches 0.154 / 0.117 (classic / e-bike); LightGBM without any station information reaches 0.090 / 0.071.
  2. [K4] The model helps most on the last bike: skill 0.182 / 0.159 with one bike now, against 0.038 / 0.039 with 6 or more.
  3. [K5] Skill grows with the horizon, from 0.079 / 0.058 at h = 2 min to 0.177 / 0.143 at h = 14 min. This is skill relative to the reference, not accuracy: the forecast itself gets less accurate further ahead (Brier 0.0103 to 0.0283, classic), and the reference loses accuracy faster (0.0112 to 0.0344).

How well it carries over, and what comes next

  1. [K6] Test is lower than validation: 0.125 / 0.092 against 0.154 / 0.117. The test days include a weekend and the validation days do not; leaving the weekend out closes 29 % / 39 % of the gap, so the weekend is about a third of the drop. Data v2 is already built with a validation week and a test week of 5 weekdays and 2 weekend days each, so the model is chosen on days that include a weekend.
  2. [K7] More training data helps, with a slowing gain (earlier count model, MSE skill, data-v1): 0.072 with 5 training days, 0.083 with 10, 0.109 with 20 (classic); about +0.019 per extra week over 10–20 days and +0.009 over 15–20. Data v2 (more days) tests this on the probability model.

Figure K-a (finding 3). [K8] Knowing the station gives most of the gain: LightGBM on growing input sets (val, seed 0); location and capacity alone recover almost all of it.

Figure K-b (findings 4 and 5). [K9] The gain is largest with one bike left (left) and grows with the horizon (right); val, mean over seeds 0–2.

Figure K-d (finding 6). [K11] The weekend days score lowest, and the test weekdays are also below the validation days (Oct 28, a partial test day of 76,559 rows, is left out).

Figure K-e (finding 7). [K12] More training days raise the validation skill, with a slowing gain (count model, skill = 1 − MSE_model / MSE_persistence, data-v1, mean ± sd over seeds 0–2).

1. Data collected¶

[D4] We poll the public Toronto Bike Share feed (GBFS) every minute since Sep 29, with backup pollers, and add Environment Canada weather. The team table (data-v1) turns the polls into rows: for each station and anchor time t (every 10 min) it draws 3 random horizons h between 2 and 15 min. Each row holds the counts now and 10 and 30 min before, the station, the time of day and the weather, and the counts at t + h. Only anchors where some count (classic bikes, e-bikes or free docks) is 2 or less are kept, so every number below is on these station-times, where a rider may find no bike or no dock. [C1] Pollers, weather source and the anchor rule as described in the team's data documentation; a coverage table (polls per day, gaps) from the data part of the team notebook should go here.

The table gives the size of each split and how often the answer changes: the flip rate is the share of rows whose 'at least one bike' status differs between t and t + h. [D5] Status flips are rare: 2.6 % of val rows for classic bikes and 4.3 % for e-bikes, so 'what you see now' is already a strong forecast.

2. Task and score¶

Output. For each bike type, p = P(at least one bike at t + h), h = 2–15 min. One model covers all stations and horizons (h is an input). Loss: binary cross-entropy. [D6] We moved from forecasting the count (with MSE) to this probability because a rider's question is 'will there be a bike?', and a probability says how sure the answer is. [C2] This replaces the team's count / MSE direction of Oct 28; the team agreed to the change at its Nov 12 meeting.

Score. The Brier score, mean (p − y)², and the Brier skill score against a reference, BSS = 1 − Brier_model / Brier_ref (0 = no better than the reference, 1 = perfect). [D7] We do not use log loss against persistence: persistence says 0 or 1, so every miss costs log(0) = infinity. The Brier score is finite for 0/1 forecasts and is still a proper score.

References, all fitted on the training days only:

Reference Forecast
Persistence 1 if a bike is there now, else 0
Calibrated persistence (headline) P(bike at t + h given the count now and h)
Station-hour look-up (added after review; val only) calibrated persistence corrected per station, hour of day and count now
Climatology the station's rate at that hour of the week, ignoring the count now

[D8] Calibrated persistence is our headline 'doing nothing': it uses only what the screen shows now, and it already knows that '1 bike now' is not a sure bike later; it beats raw persistence by 0.061 / 0.065 (classic / e-bike, val). The station-hour look-up is a stronger bar that needs a table per station and hour: it scores 0.115 / 0.085 against calibrated persistence. It was added after the test read, so it has no test score. Climatology ignores the count now and is far weaker (BSS against persistence -4.51 / -3.93).

Method: the score (score_prob.py)

def brier(p, y):
    """Mean squared error of the probability, per target column."""
    return ((np.asarray(p, np.float64) - y) ** 2).mean(axis=0)

def bss(p, p_ref, y):
    """Brier skill score of p against the reference p_ref, per target column."""
    return 1 - brier(p, y) / brier(p_ref, y)

Method: the headline reference, fitted on the training rows only

class CalibratedPersistence:
    """p = P(y = 1 | min(count now, CAP), h_target) from the train rows, per target, shrunk toward the count's rate.
    A (count, h) cell missing from train falls back to the count's rate over all h."""

    def fit(self, df):
        y = labels(df)
        self.table = {}
        for i, x in enumerate(TARGETS):
            c = np.minimum(df[f"{x}_now"].to_numpy(), CAP).astype(int)
            g = pd.DataFrame({"c": c, "h": df.h_target.to_numpy().astype(int), "y": y[:, i]})
            by_c = g.groupby("c").y.mean()
            cell = g.groupby(["c", "h"]).y.agg(["sum", "size"])
            prior = by_c.reindex(cell.index.get_level_values("c")).to_numpy()
            self.table[x] = ((cell["sum"] + K * prior) / (cell["size"] + K)).rename("p")
            self.table[x + "_by_c"] = by_c
            self.table[x + "_cmax"] = int(c.max())
        return self

    def predict(self, df):
        out = np.empty((len(df), len(TARGETS)))
        h = df.h_target.to_numpy().astype(int)
        for i, x in enumerate(TARGETS):  # a count above any count seen in train takes the top cell
            c = np.minimum(df[f"{x}_now"].to_numpy(), self.table[x + "_cmax"]).astype(int)
            idx = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays([c, h], names=["c", "h"])
            p = self.table[x].reindex(idx).to_numpy().copy()
            miss = np.isnan(p)  # a (count, h) cell not in train: the count's rate over all h
            p[miss] = self.table[x + "_by_c"].reindex(c[miss]).to_numpy()
            out[:, i] = p
        assert not np.isnan(out).any(), "calibrated persistence: a count now never seen in train"
        return out

3. Model¶

Label and inputs. The label of bike type x is y = 1 if the count of x at t + h is at least 1. [D9] The network takes the table's 20 numeric inputs: horizon h; classic, e-bike and free-dock counts now, 10 and 30 min ago; capacity; latitude and longitude; hour of day (sine and cosine); weekend; temperature; humidity; and two of them, renting_now and returning_now, are station-status flags ('accepts rentals / returns'), equal to 1 on every training and validation row, so they are constant and carry no information (18 inputs vary). They are standardised with the training mean and standard deviation. An 8-number embedding of the station is learned with the model. Two outputs give one logit per bike type.

Method: the label

def labels(df):
    """1 if at least one bike of the type is at the station at t + h. [n, len(TARGETS)] float64"""
    return df[[f"y_{x}" for x in TARGETS]].to_numpy(np.float64)

Method: the network (37_model_search.py; config of the chosen model: Config(arch='mlp', depth=2, width=256, emb=8, gru=0, lr=0.001, batch=4096, dropout=0.3, wd=0.0))

class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, cfg, n_inputs, n_stations):
        super().__init__()
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.station = nn.Embedding(n_stations + 1, cfg.emb)
        if cfg.arch == "gru":
            self.rnn = nn.GRU(len(SEQ[0]) + len(SEQ), cfg.gru, batch_first=True)
            self.register_buffer("seq_idx", torch.tensor(SEQ_IDX))
            self.register_buffer("ctx_idx", torch.tensor(CTX_IDX))
            self.register_buffer("step_onehot", torch.eye(len(SEQ)))
            n_in = len(CTX_IDX) + cfg.gru + cfg.emb
        else:
            n_in = n_inputs + cfg.emb
        layers = []
        for _ in range(cfg.depth):
            layers += [nn.Linear(n_in, cfg.width), nn.ReLU()]
            if cfg.dropout > 0:
                layers.append(nn.Dropout(cfg.dropout))
            n_in = cfg.width
        layers.append(nn.Linear(n_in, len(TARGETS)))
        self.net = nn.Sequential(*layers)

    def forward(self, x, station):
        e = self.station(station)
        if self.cfg.arch == "gru":
            seq = x[:, self.seq_idx]  # [n, 3 steps, 3 counts]
            seq = torch.cat([seq, self.step_onehot.expand(len(x), -1, -1)], dim=2)
            _, hT = self.rnn(seq)
            return self.net(torch.cat([x[:, self.ctx_idx], hT[0], e], dim=1))
        return self.net(torch.cat([x, e], dim=1))

Method: training (condensed from train() in 46_prob_search.py). Adam, learning rate 10⁻³, batch 4,096, one pass over the 7,525,845 training rows per epoch, up to 30 epochs; keep the epoch with the lowest validation cross-entropy; stop after 3 epochs without improvement.

model = Net(cfg, n_inputs=20, n_stations=1071)          # one extra embedding row for unseen stations
opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
loss_fn = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()                         # binary cross-entropy on the 2 logits
best, best_epoch = inf, 0
for epoch in range(1, 31):
    model.train()
    for idx in torch.randperm(len(x_train)).split(4096):
        loss = loss_fn(model(x_train[idx], station_train[idx]), y_train[idx])
        opt.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); opt.step()
    val = cross_entropy(sigmoid(model(x_val, station_val)), y_val)
    if val < best:
        best, best_epoch, best_state = val, epoch, copy(model.state_dict())
    elif epoch - best_epoch >= 3:                        # patience 3
        break
model.load_state_dict(best_state)

4. Step by step: from references to the chosen model (validation days)¶

We trained four networks with three seeds each (0, 1, 2), so a gap between models can be judged against the spread over seeds, plus LightGBM (gradient-boosted trees, three seeds) and logistic regression. Validation: Oct 19–23. The rule to pick the model was fixed before any run: the lowest validation Brier (mean of the two bike types), preferring a network with fewer parameters if it is within noise.

Result. [D10] The models that know the station all clear the bar by about the same amount. The chosen MLP 2×256, dropout 0.3 scores 0.154 ± 0.0002 (classic) and 0.117 ± 0.0006 (e-bike; ± = sd over seeds); the other networks and LightGBM are within 0.0085 of it. The day-to-day spread is larger than the seed spread: over the five validation days the chosen model ranges 0.146–0.163 (classic) and 0.112–0.121 (e-bike).

[D11] What the gain needs (LightGBM, seed 0, one input set at a time; table below): the counts now and h alone give 0.011 / 0.006; adding the lag counts gives 0.080 / 0.061; all inputs without any station information (no station index, location or capacity) give 0.090 / 0.071; with the location and capacity but no station index 0.148 / 0.112; with the station but without the lag counts 0.150 / 0.113. So the station (its location is enough) is the largest part of the gain, and once the station is known the lag counts add little. Logistic regression, which has neither the station nor a non-linear use of the inputs, only matches calibrated persistence (-0.000 / 0.002).

[D12] The rule picked MLP 2×256, dropout 0.3. Its lead is small. Gaps against calibrated persistence, classic / e-bike, with z = gap / √(seed variance + station-sampling variance): over dropout 0.1 +0.0010 / +0.0012 (z 1.6 / 2.1, a tie: same size, and the rule cannot separate them); over the GRU +0.0014 / +0.0019 (z 1.4 / 3.1); over LightGBM +0.0031 / +0.0034 (z 2.6 / 4.6); over the base 2×64 +0.0085 / +0.0034 (z 2.1 / 2.0). With 3 seeds per model these z values are rough. The candidates were picked from the count search on the same validation days. [D13] Part of the base's gap was early stopping: rerun with patience 6 (after the reviews), its seeds stop at epochs 25/19/24 and reach 0.150 / 0.115, against 0.145 / 0.114 with patience 3. The rule would still keep MLP 2×256, dropout 0.3 (gap 0.000084 in mean Brier against a threshold of 0.000063); the choice is not changed, since the test days were already read.

5. Where the model helps, and is it calibrated? (validation days)¶

[D14] Measured as skill, the model helps most when one bike is left: BSS 0.182 (classic) and 0.159 (e-bike) against calibrated persistence, against 0.038 / 0.039 with 6 or more bikes (on test: 0.145 / 0.123 at one bike). Stations with no bike now matter as much for classic bikes: there the question is whether a bike will arrive. The gain also grows with the horizon, from 0.079 / 0.058 at h = 2 min to 0.177 / 0.143 at h = 14 min. The forecast itself gets less accurate with h (Brier 0.0103 to 0.0283, classic), but calibrated persistence degrades faster (0.0112 to 0.0344), so the gain over it grows. [D15] Share of the total Brier reduction against calibrated persistence: rows with 0 bikes now give 46 % (classic) / 37 % (e-bike), rows with 1 bike 47 % / 59 %.

[D16] In rider terms (validation only): when one bike is there now, it is gone by t + h in 7.6 % of cases (classic; 9.2 % for e-bikes). A warning on the 10 % of these cases with the lowest forecast would catch 48 % of the times the bike is gone (41 % for e-bikes), and be right 36 % / 37 % of the time, so about 2 in 3 warnings would be false alarms. Ranking within each horizon gives nearly the same catch (46 % / 38 %). The same warning from calibrated persistence catches 13 % / 14 %, and from the station-hour look-up 43 % / 36 %. The base MLP and LightGBM catch about as much as the chosen model, so this is a property of the models that know the station, not of this one.

[D17] On the validation days the forecasts are well calibrated: in every bin with at least 1,000 rows the observed share is within 0.010 (classic) and 0.015 (e-bike) of the forecast (seed 0; the epoch was picked on these days, so this is a best case). Climatology is not calibrated (off by up to 0.24 for e-bikes, all rows): each of its station × hour-of-week cells holds only 2.7 training days on average, and with 10 times more shrinkage its e-bike gap falls to 0.08. Its high Brier score comes from ignoring the count now: more shrinkage lowers it only from 0.210 to 0.198 (e-bike).

[D18] The test days (Oct 24–28) were read once for this model, for the chosen model only, after the choice; the protocol was committed before the read. The same days had been scored once before (Nov 12, early morning) for our earlier count models; nothing in this search was chosen on them. Nothing was tuned after the read.

[D19] The gain holds on test but is smaller: 0.125 / 0.092 against calibrated persistence (validation 0.154 / 0.117) and 0.172 / 0.144 against persistence. Calibration is looser than on validation, in a systematic way: classic forecasts of 0.1–0.4 are 0.012–0.029 too high, e-bike forecasts of 0.4–0.7 0.018–0.022 too low. Calibrated persistence stays within 0.006 / 0.005. [C3] About a third of the drop is the weekend: the test week starts on a Saturday and the validation days have no weekend. Weekends are harder even on the training days (in sample: weekdays 0.166, Saturdays 0.134, Sundays 0.128, classic). On test, Sat–Sun pooled give 0.114 / 0.081 and Mon–Tue 0.134 / 0.102; leaving the weekend out closes 29 % (classic) and 39 % (e-bike) of the gap to validation. The test weekdays are still below every validation day. The test week also has fewer flips (2.2 % against 2.6 %, classic), and the model's Brier score itself is lower on test (0.0186 against 0.0210): the reference improved more than the model. Calmer days tend to score lower (table above), but that is not all of it: the test Monday, with the same classic flip rate as the validation Monday (2.51 % against 2.51 %), still scores 0.140 against 0.149. Untested: how much is the calmer week and how much the distance from training (test days are 6–10 days after it, validation days 1–5). [D20] Oct 28 holds only the early-morning hours (76,559 rows). Dropping the 2,324 test rows at stations never seen in training changes the skill by at most 0.0002. The station-hour look-up was added after the test read and has no test score.

7. Preliminary: data v2¶

[D21] A second, larger table (data v2) adds the days to Nov 10: 11,198,091 training rows (to 2026-10-27), and a validation week (2026-10-28 to 2026-11-03) and test week (2026-11-04 to 2026-11-10) of 5 weekdays and 2 weekend days each. Its validation week overlaps the data-v1 test days, so its numbers are not a second data-v1 test; its own test week has not been read. So far only a 1-epoch smoke test has run, with the earlier count target (MSE): its skill is 1 − MSE_model / MSE_persistence, not the Brier skill above, and only shows that the pipeline runs end to end.

8. What is left, and is it feasible?¶

[D22] Done: data collection (running since Sep 29), the dataset, the score and its references, a small model search, and a test score. Left, in order:

  1. [D23] Data v2 (Nov 16–19): retrain the chosen model and the station-hour look-up on the larger table and check the weekend days on its validation week.
  2. [D24] Longer history (Nov 19–22): give the GRU 60 min of past counts, which data v2 provides; freeze the final model on Nov 22 and score it once on the unread data-v2 test week (Nov 4–10).
  3. [D25] Rider-level evaluation (Nov 23–29): turn the probabilities into advice (e.g. 'go elsewhere' below a threshold) and count strandings avoided and false alarms per 100 trips.
  4. [D26] Video (Dec 6) and final report (Dec 11).

[D27] Compute is not the limit: the 16 runs of this search took 3.8 h of run time, 0.9 h of wall time with several runs in parallel on one laptop; data v2 has 1.5 times the rows, so the same search should take about 1.3 h. The person time is the limit: [C4] about 5 h per person per week (the team's budget from the proposal) leaves room for steps 1–3 if each person takes one.
